entries.appliesTo: any person using a child's image to train an AI model to produce child sexual abuse materials

sources.prohibition: R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3) — 'to use an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created with the intent to train an artificial intelligence model to produce child sexual abuse materials'
sources.coveredSubjects: R.S. 14:81.1(A)(3) — 'an image of a child under the age of seventeen years at the time the image was created'

flags: age threshold is 17, not 18 — ai-crimes family has no ageThreshold param; captured only as coveredSubjects=minors (quote: 'a child under the age of seventeen years')

R.S. 14:81.1(A)(4) removes the natural-person element: 'It is not a required element of an offense under this Section that the child depicted in the child sexual abuse materials be a natural person' — extends the offense to AI-generated/virtual depictions
no penalty provision in this act's text — fines/imprisonment live in unamended subsections of existing R.S. 14:81.1, so exposure is omitted (rule 3/4)

amended R.S. 14:81.1(G) adds trier-of-fact factors for whether 'the image used to train an artificial intelligence model depicts a person who appears to be under the age of seventeen years' — evidentiary provision, no coded duty
